chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad al-Hanaat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who reneged from Islam, for whom would his inheritance be? He said: His inheritance is distributed among his heirs according to the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
ai.seo_question: What happens to the inheritance of a Muslim who apostatizes?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that apostasy does not sever familial ties for inheritance purposes, distinguishing this view from schools that exclude apostates entirely. This ruling emphasizes that the estate is distributed among heirs according to the Quranic shares, reflecting the principle that apostasy is a personal spiritual breach rather than a total civil disinheritance. This perspective is significant in Shia jurisprudence for maintaining the continuity of family wealth distribution despite the individual's change in religious status.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abu Wallad Al Hanaat, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who reneged (go back on) from Al-Islam, for whom would his inheritance happen to be?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘His inheritance would be distributed over his inheritors upon the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahf ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from abu Wallad al-Hannat who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who has turned away from Islam and about who inherits him.
He (the Imam) said, ‘His legacy is distributed according to the book of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious.’”
